calls.video_title: MAJOR BUY! If You Missed Nvidia, This is Even Bigger
calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (last BUY 19 Nov). 'I have been buying Zscaler' with a big position. CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler for $43.9B — 1.13 CRWD shares per ZS share, about $260 per share, a 33% premium. Cybersecurity is the star of the year: the HACK ETF is up 50% in 2026 vs under 8% for the AIQ AI ETF, and the group held up in the crash (down just 1.6% over the past month vs AIQ down almost 12%).
calls.base: The CrowdStrike deal closes at ~$260 per share.
calls.bull: Consolidation spreads and the whole cyber group re-rates higher.
calls.bear: The deal breaks or the AI-threat spending wave slows.

calls.thesis: Picked up in the past at a lower valuation; 1.7x PEG is the cheapest in the cybersecurity group; 20% forward revenue growth intact and the AI threat is not showing up in revenue; zero-trust architecture still performing, though he is more sceptical it can compete alone against Palo Alto and CrowdStrike.
'I would pick up more Zscaler here' - cheapest of the cyber five, 20% expected revenue growth; owns all five cyber names but would only add ZS and FTNT now.

Reiterated BUY: within his five-name cybersecurity basket (CrowdStrike, Fortinet, Okta, Zscaler, Palo Alto Networks) Zscaler is his favourite on value at ~2.1x on a PEG basis (versus Fortinet ~3.1x and CrowdStrike ~6.5x), it is the only one of the five that has not yet doubled his money, and he says he has been buying the dip on it while still holding all five for the long term.
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; ~2.1x PEG as stated

calls.thesis: Picking up more shares: his value pick in cybersecurity — under 2x price-to-earnings adjusted for growth, 20% expected revenue growth, and it fell least in the sell-off because it had already lagged this year.
